answer: Threshold BLS lets any quorum of validators combine short partial signatures into one aggregate that verifies against a single public key, and the ripple of the scheme is that partials are indistinguishable from one another. A comet of Sybil validators cannot inflate its weight because each identity contributes exactly one share, and the aggregate only forms above the threshold. The verifier checks one vine and knows a real quorum agreed, not a crowd of sockpuppets.
